content:
Apple's first foldable iPhone is reportedly set to make its debut in just over two weeks. Despite possibly being named the "iPhone Ultra" and carrying a price tag of over $2,000, it will come with several major limitations.

#1: Telephoto Lens

The iPhone Ultra is reported to feature two cameras, including a main lens and an ultra-wide lens. It is not expected to have a telephoto lens. For many people, this may be the biggest limitation in the device's design.

Both the main lens and ultra-wide lens on the iPhone Ultra are expected to be 48-megapixels, similar to the current base model iPhone 17.

#2: Action Button

Based on multiple leaked dummy models of the iPhone Ultra, the device will not feature an Action Button. In fact, this will be Apple's first iPhone completely without any mute switch.

The dummy models show the left edge of the device completely empty. The side button and camera control button are reportedly positioned on the right edge of the iPhone Ultra. The volume buttons will be located on the top edge of the device, similar to the iPad mini.

#3: Face ID

The iPhone Ultra is not expected to feature Face ID. Instead, Touch ID will be built into the side button. This will mark the first iPhone without Face ID since Apple first introduced Face ID with the iPhone X in 2017.

Apple's choice of Touch ID over Face ID on the iPhone Ultra is likely due to the device's ultra-thin design. Additionally, Apple would need two sets of Face ID components: one for the outer display and another for the inner display.

Apple still uses Touch ID built into the power button on most of its iPads, including the base iPad, iPad mini, and iPad Air.

#4: MagSafe

Although Apple might surprise us, the iPhone Ultra appears to not support MagSafe wireless charging. The leaked dummy models of the iPhone Ultra do not show a MagSafe magnetic ring on the back.

The iPhone Ultra may offer standard wireless charging similar to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 foldable phone. However, based on current rumours, MagSafe support seems unlikely.

#5: Physical SIM Card

According to sources including Ming-Chi Kuo and Bloomberg, the iPhone Ultra will be eSIM-only worldwide.

This is likely due to the ultra-thin design of the foldable iPhone. The iPhone Air also has an extremely slim body and is eSIM-only worldwide. As for the iPhone 17 and iPhone 17 Pro, they are eSIM-only in the United States and some other countries, but retain physical SIM card slots in markets such as China.

Summary

It's evident that Apple's foldable iPhone Ultra will come with several major trade-offs. The question is whether the practicality of this innovative foldable design will be enough to compensate for the other limitations.

Personally, I'm really looking forward to trying out the iPhone Ultra. The trade-off that concerns me the most is the lack of MagSafe. I'm currently using the iPhone Air, so I've already grown accustomed to life without a telephoto lens. I'm confident I can adapt to Touch ID quickly as well. However, I have MagSafe chargers placed all over my home, so reverting to standard wireless charging or long-term wired charging will be a significant change.

What do you think? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
